findings.title: Salesforce refresh uses undefined prisma
findings.body: The newly added refresh block calls `prisma.credential.update` but this file never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. When this code runs, it will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined`, and the project should also fail type-checking. Add the missing import.

findings.title: Google refresh stores Zod SafeParse result instead of token data
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), but here `key` is that wrapper and is written to the credential directly. After a successful Google refresh, the DB key becomes `{ success: true, data: { ...tokens } }`; subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in the constructor fails, breaking the Google Calendar integration. Use `refreshTokenResponse.data` here.

findings.title: Minimum token schema does not validate or retain expiry fields
findings.body: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` both resolve to the same string (`[object Object]`), so the schema effectively only requires `access_token` and drops or fails to validate all other token fields. When credential sharing is enabled, any caller using this branch parses a token response into essentially `{ access_token }`, losing `expires_in`/`expiry_date`, `instance_url`, and other fields. The intended numeric expiry validation is never performed.

findings.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with string "refresh_token"
findings.body: When a parsed refresh response does not include `refresh_token`, this mutates `data.refresh_token` to the literal text `"refresh_token"`. Callers like Office365 and Zoom then persist that value over the user's real refresh token, so later refreshes fail. Do not synthesize a placeholder; preserve the existing credential refresh token in the caller.

findings.title: Sync token refresh returns an unnormalized Response
findings.body: In sync mode this returns the raw `fetch` `Response`. Existing callers expect provider/axios-shaped values: Google reads `res.data.access_token`, HubSpot expects `.expiresIn`, and Zoho/Bigin expect `tokenInfo.data`. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, those code paths get `undefined` or missing properties and fail. Parse the JSON and return a consistent shape such as `{ data }`, or update every caller to consume `Response`.

findings.title: Credential sync endpoint receives no authentication
findings.body: The `fetch` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body. There is no secret, signature, or API key. Anyone who can reach the sync endpoint can request access tokens for arbitrary Cal.com user IDs. Since this endpoint returns third-party credentials, add an authenticated header/shared secret and enforce HTTPS.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends credential.id as calcomUserId
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens`'s third argument is supposed to be the Cal.com user ID, but this call passes `credentialId` (the credential row ID). When credential sharing is enabled, the parent app receives the DB credential ID as `calcomUserId` and may update the wrong user or fail to find the user. Pass `credential.userId` through to `refreshAccessToken`.

findings.title: Salesforce token parsing switches on global sharing flag despite fetching Salesforce directly
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)` chooses the minimal schema whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is set, even though this method always calls `login.salesforce.com` directly and never uses `refreshOAuthTokens`. Enabling credential sharing therefore makes Salesforce token parsing drop required fields such as `instance_url`, `id`, `issued_at`, `signature`, `scope`, and `token_type`; the stored DB key becomes incomplete and future connections can break.

findings.title: Refreshed Salesforce token is not used for the connection
findings.body: The method fetches and parses a new access token, but `new jsforce.Connection(...)` is created with `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.refresh_token`, not the newly parsed token. The service instance therefore starts with the old/expired access token, causing avoidable 401s or reliance on jsforce's own auto-refresh. Use the new access token and instance URL from the refresh response.

findings.title: Credential sync can create duplicate credentials under concurrent requests
findings.body: The handler does `findFirst` and then either `update` or `create` in separate queries. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both miss the existing row and insert duplicates. There is also no deterministic choice if multiple rows exist. Use a transaction plus a unique constraint/upsert keyed by `(userId, appId, type)`.

findings.title: Sync update does not mark credential valid again
findings.body: When updating an existing credential, only `key` is changed. If that credential was previously marked `invalid: true` (for example after an invalid_grant failure), it remains invalid after syncing fresh credentials and may be skipped by integrations. The update should set `invalid: false` to reflect the new source-of-truth credential.

findings.title: Office 365 video sync refresh can overwrite stored credential with an incomplete token
findings.body: When sync mode returns the documented generic payload (`access_token` plus expiry date), `responseBody.expires_in` is undefined, so `expiry_date` is set to `Date.now()` (immediately expired), and the whole `responseBody` is stored as the key. The existing `refresh_token`, `token_type`, `scope`, and `email` are not preserved, so later refreshes fail. This integration needs to merge the sync response into the existing credential instead of replacing it.

findings.title: Invalid webhook body causes unhandled ZodError
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` is not wrapped in try/catch and no method check is performed. A POST with a malformed body, or a GET where `req.body` is absent, throws a `ZodError`, producing a generic 500 instead of a controlled 400. Use `safeParse` and explicitly reject non-POST methods.

findings.title: AES-256 key generation command yields 24 bytes, not 32
findings.body: The comment says the key must be 32 bytes for AES-256 and suggests `openssl rand -base64 24`. Base64-decoding 24 input bytes yields a 24-byte key, not 32. Users following this instruction will configure an invalid/weak key. Suggest `openssl rand -base64 32` or `openssl rand -hex 32`.

findings.title: No tests for credential sync webhook or token refresh helpers
findings.body: The PR adds a security-sensitive webhook, encryption/decryption path, and shared OAuth refresh/parsing helpers used by many integrations. The checklist explicitly says no tests were added. Given the parser shape mismatches and data-loss issues, tests for success, invalid secret, malformed payload, existing/update, and sync vs local refresh would catch regressions.
